---
title: "Patch main figure — pathway analysis (Figure 6)"
---

## Overview

Compose the main pathway analysis figure (Figure 6): gene upset plot (a), GO term upset plot (b), and function categorization barplot (c) at publication column width.

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
#| echo: false

pacman::p_load(patchwork, ggtext, install = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: load-theme
#| echo: false

source(here("custom_func/theme_main_fig.R"))
set_pub_geom_defaults()
```

## Load Plot Objects

Load pre-generated RDS plot objects for the top 1000 CpG pathway analysis.

```{r}
#| label: load-plots

panel_a <- read_rds(
  here("pathway_analysis/01_genes/output/top1000_all_genes_upset_plot.rds")
)

panel_b <- read_rds(
  here("pathway_analysis/03_transition_specific_GO_terms/output/top1000_condition_specific_GO_terms.rds")
)

panel_c <- read_rds(
  here("pathway_analysis/04_function_categorization/output/top1000_barplot_function_category.rds")
)
```

## Modify Panels

Apply publication theme and rescale elements for 6.5" column width.

```{r}
#| label: modify-panels

# Panels A & b: upset plots — use & to propagate theme to internal sub-plots
panel_a <- panel_a & theme_main_fig()
panel_b <- panel_b & theme_main_fig()

# Panel C: function categorization barplot — angled axis labels, blank y title
panel_c <- panel_c +
  theme_main_fig() +
  theme(
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_markdown(angle = 15)
  )
```

## Compose with Patchwork

Arrange panels in a 2-column layout: a and b on the top row, c spanning the two rows below.

```{r}
#| label: compose-figure
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 9

layout <- "
AAABBB
CCCCCC
CCCCCC
"

fig_pathway_analysis <-
  free(panel_a) +
  free(panel_b) +
  free(panel_c) +
  plot_layout(design = layout, guides = "auto", axes = "keep", axis_titles = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")

fig_pathway_analysis
```

## Save Figure

Save at publication dimensions (600 DPI). Height is 6.75" rather than the former 9": panel D occupied
one of the layout's four row-units (c spans two), so dropping it scales the canvas by 3/4 and leaves
a, b and c at exactly their previous physical size.

```{r}
#| label: save-figure
fs::dir_create(here("pathway_analysis/05_patch_fig_and_make_table/output"))


png(here("pathway_analysis/05_patch_fig_and_make_table/output/fig_pathway_analysis.png"),
    width = 7.5, height = 6.75, units = "in", res = 600)
fig_pathway_analysis
dev.off()
```

## Verify Output

Confirm output file was created successfully.

```{r}
#| label: verify-output

fs::file_info(here("pathway_analysis/05_patch_fig_and_make_table/output/fig_pathway_analysis.png")) |>
  select(path, size, modification_time)
```
